title: Work-item hierarchy query and the reverse-parent index — plan 002
epic_title: Carina — work-item hierarchy query and the reverse-parent index

tasks.title: Stand up the reverse-parent marker index and maintain it at the choke point
tasks.goal: The store keeps a derived reverse-parent index — one zero-byte marker per parent→child edge, sharded under a gitignored directory — current at the single parent-mutation choke point and rebuildable in full from the item files alone.
tasks.current: The child's stored `parent` is the only record of an edge; the reverse direction is a full-store scan and no reverse index exists on disk.
tasks.desired: Creating a child with a parent, reparenting, and clearing a parent each write or remove exactly one marker, and only after the authoritative item write has committed (field-first), under the child's existing per-item lock. Markers are empty — membership is presence — so the index can only lag, never hold a wrong value. The index directory is gitignored and never committed. A rebuild reconstructs the whole index purely from the item `parent` fields, and a read finding the index absent triggers that build. Concurrent parent-writes to different children under one parent touch disjoint marker files and lose none.
scope: the sharded per-edge marker layout and the gitignore entry that keeps it out of version control
incremental one-marker maintenance inside the set-parent / clear-parent / create choke point, ordered strictly after the item write
the pure rebuild-from-item-fields primitive and the lazy build invoked when the index is absent
the disjoint-file property under concurrent parent-writes
out_of_scope: the parent→children query surface and read modes (T2)
the operator-facing recovery verb, the dirty-check trigger, and crash recovery (T3)
acceptance: after a create-with-parent, a reparent, and a clear, the reverse index lists exactly each parent's current children and the vacated edge's marker is gone
the index directory never appears in git status, and a rebuild from an empty index reconstructs every edge from the item files alone
a marker operation is observed only after the item write has committed, verified by a stop injected between the two writes
concurrent parent-writes to different children under one parent complete with no lost marker and touch disjoint files
key_interfaces: the marker path and shard helpers, and the gitignored index root beside `items/`
the edge-maintenance hook invoked from within the existing parent mutation, after the atomic item write
the rebuild-from-truth primitive that derives the whole index from the item `parent` fields

tasks.title: Parent→children query: the shared O(k) enumerator and `list --parent`
tasks.goal: A work item's direct children are queryable in time bounded by the child count through one implementation shared by the port and the `carina list --parent` CLI, with a display mode that trusts the index and a decision mode that re-verifies each candidate's authoritative parent.
tasks.current: Children are found by scanning and filtering every item (bounded by the whole store); `Children` takes only a parent id, there is no parent filter on the list surface, and there is no display-versus-decision distinction.
tasks.desired: A parent-scoped query returns exactly the given item's direct children, all states by default, narrowable by the existing state, signal, and role filters, and byte-identical from the CLI and the port; a parent with no children returns empty, not an error. Lookup reads the parent's markers and then each named child's authoritative file, so latency stays flat as the total item count grows with a fixed child count, with no full-corpus scan on the query path. A decision-mode read re-reads each candidate's `parent` field and drops any that no longer names this parent; a display-mode read trusts the markers. A read that finds the index absent builds it first.
scope: the shared child enumerator over the marker index, carrying the display and decision read modes
the parent filter on the list query, composing with the state, signal, and role filters
the `carina list --parent` surface with machine output, byte-identical to the port
the read-time lazy build when the index is absent
out_of_scope: the grouped epic rollup and the `show` surface (T4)
the operator-facing recovery verb and the dirty-check trigger (T3)
acceptance: a parent-scoped list returns exactly the item's direct children in every state, byte-identical from the CLI and the port; a state filter narrows to the expected members; a childless parent returns empty
children-query latency stays flat as total item count grows across the capacity range at fixed child count, with no full-corpus scan on the path
a decision-mode read drops a stale or hand-edited marker by re-verifying each candidate's parent, while a display-mode read over the same store still lists it
a query run against an absent index builds the index and returns the correct children
key_interfaces: `Children` — the enumerator gains a child filter and a read-mode argument, one implementation over the index
the read-mode selector distinguishing a display read from a decision read
the list query's parent field composing with state, signal, and role
the `carina list --parent` verb and its machine output

tasks.title: `reindex`: the sole drift recovery, dirty-check, and crash restoration
tasks.goal: A single reindex operation rebuilds the reverse index wholly from the item files — the only drift recovery — exposed as `carina reindex`, healing a torn item-then-marker pair or a hand-edit, and gated by a cheap dirty check before an exact read.
tasks.current: The rebuild-from-truth primitive exists (T1) but is not reachable as a verb, has no trigger beyond first-use absence, and no crash or hand-edit recovery is demonstrated.
tasks.desired: `carina reindex` rebuilds the index from the item `parent` fields and reports its trigger, its item and marker counts, and its duration. A crash injected between the item write and the marker operation leaves the item correct and the index stale by one edge, which reindex restores. A hand-edited `parent` that bypassed the CLI trips a cheap dirty check that rebuilds the index before the next exact read. Recovery is always a full rebuild — no incremental self-correction path exists.
scope: the `carina reindex` verb over the rebuild primitive, reporting trigger, item and marker counts, and duration
crash-injection recovery across the item-then-marker cut point
the dirty-check signal that gates a rebuild before an exact read, healing a hand-edit
the reindex and fault conformance rows
out_of_scope: any incremental self-correction of the index — recovery is a full rebuild by design
the enumerator, list, and rollup surfaces (T2, T4)
acceptance: `carina reindex` reconstructs the index to match the item files and reports its trigger, its item and marker counts, and its duration
a crash injected between the item write and the marker operation leaves the item correct, and reindex restores the missing marker
a hand-edited parent trips the dirty check and a rebuild heals the index before the next exact read
the only recovery path is a full rebuild — no incremental self-correction exists (inspection)
key_interfaces: the reindex operation reporting its trigger, counts, and duration
the `carina reindex` verb and its machine output
the dirty-check signal comparing index freshness against the item tree
tasks.overlap_accepted: parallel branch over the store, kit, and CLI packages; the recovery verb, its conformance rows, and its fault fixtures each land in their own file — extension is by new file, not shared-line append (AP-27) — so the lone shared registration line is the only contended edit and falls to the recovery loop

tasks.title: The epic rollup grouped by open and closed (`show`)
tasks.goal: An epic's `show` reports its children grouped into open and closed sets — the all-states rollup — computed over the shared child enumerator, replacing today's open-only rollup so a completed epic still surfaces its full task set.
tasks.current: The rollup derives only the open children from a `Children` scan, so `show <epic>` omits closed children and a completed epic's task set is reachable only by grepping the item files.
tasks.desired: `show <epic>` reports its children grouped into open and closed sets — the count and identity of each — computed over the one shared child enumerator, so the port's rollup and the CLI agree. The grouping matches a hand-computed expectation over a fixture corpus, and a completed epic surfaces its full closed task set through the rollup.
scope: the rollup over the shared enumerator returning open and closed child groups
the `carina show` grouped presentation replacing the open-only rollup
the rollup conformance row against a fixture corpus
out_of_scope: any richer traversal — transitive descendants, ancestor chains, cross-repo hierarchy — which a future design owns
any auto-close sweep of an epic from its children's states
acceptance: `show <epic>` reports its children grouped into open and closed sets, count and identity each, matching a hand-computed expectation over a fixture corpus
the rollup is computed over the one shared child enumerator, and the port's rollup and the CLI return the same grouped result
a completed epic surfaces its full closed task set through the rollup rather than an empty open-only view
key_interfaces: the rollup returning the open and closed child groups over the shared enumerator
the `carina show` grouped output replacing the open-only rollup
